description: Two-head configuration over one 8700-D feature space: seven annotation blocks (8604 columns) plus two co-essentiality blocks (96 columns). Frozen from the sealed champion; no parameter is a selection rule.

comparison_baseline.label: old TusoPerturb
comparison_baseline.what_it_is: The frozen per-benchmark head table of the TusoPerturb codebase as it stood when the sealed run was executed: perturbhd_hit on the v1.0.0 hit configuration (8608-D shared stack, RidgeCV, k=13 neighbours, unsigned top-2% binary arm); the four other slots on the Systema head configuration (three-arm blend, residual-over-pert-mean target) reading the 8604-D annotation stack.
comparison_baseline.differs_from_v1_0_0_release: Yes, for cellsim / scperturb / perturbhd_reg. The v1.0.0 release ran a different config on those three slots; it was replaced on 2026-08-04 after a pre-registered 2x2 transfer test (feature stack x head, 4 datasets, fold-0 held out, 3 seeds on perturbhd_reg) in which the transferred head swept 12/12 headline metrics with no magnitude-metric regression. The sealed comparison therefore runs against the stronger of the two old tables, not the weaker published one.

protocol.split: sealed held-out test, read exactly once
protocol.placeholder_reason: systema composite_dev is a harness bookkeeping field, not a model-discriminating score; it is recorded but excluded from every count.
protocol.value_reported: mean over seeds; sd is the across-seed standard deviation

verification.config_fidelity: all 21 HeadConfig fields of both shipped heads compared field-by-field against the resolved sealed champion: 21/21 match
verification.feature_parity: shipped build_features vs the sealed feature path on 4 PerturbHD datasets, 2 hit subsets and 3 Systema panels: max abs diff 0.0
verification.prediction_parity: shipped head_predict vs the sealed implementation on identical inputs, shared head in both batch modes and hit head: max abs diff 0.0

determinism.env: OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell set before the first numpy import
